s0103.literal: Editorial footnote marker 7. We your ministers jointly recommend that, according to the present case, Fangtai be removed from the posts he holds and that the Director of the Imperial Clan be ordered to strip his nobility and fief.
s0103.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 7. We jointly recommend that, on the facts before us, Fangtai be dismissed from office and the Director of the Imperial Clan be ordered to strip his title and fief.

s0104.literal: Respectfully we report on white tablets.

s0106.literal: Soon his former offices and title were restored.
s0106.idiomatic: Before long his offices and title were restored.

s0107.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, his general's title unchanged.
s0107.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenming era he was made attendant-in-ordinary, keeping his general's rank.

s0108.literal: In year three, Sui forces crossed the Yangzi; Fangtai, together with Fan Meng, General of Loyal Martial Might and Inspector of South Yuzhou, and Jiang Yuansun, General of the Left Guard, led the navy at Baixia to move back and forth cutting off the river route.
s0108.idiomatic: In year three the Sui army crossed the Yangzi; Fangtai joined Fan Meng, loyal-martial general and inspector of South Yuzhou, and Jiang Yuansun of the Left Guard in leading a fleet at Baixia to block the river line.

s0109.literal: Sui sent the campaign marshal and chief clerk Gao Jiong to lead ships upstream against them; Meng and Yuansun both surrendered, Fangtai's officers and soldiers scattered, and he abandoned his ships and fled.
s0109.idiomatic: Sui sent Gao Jiong with a fleet upstream; Fan and Jiang surrendered, Fangtai's men scattered, and he abandoned his ships and fled.

s0110.literal: When the capital fell, he entered the Pass together with the Last Emperor.
s0110.idiomatic: When the capital fell he was taken to the north with the Last Emperor.

s0111.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he was Director of the Palace Ladies.
s0111.idiomatic: Under Sui's Daye reign he served as director of the palace ladies.

s0113.literal: Fangqing in youth was clear and alert and widely read books and histories.
s0113.idiomatic: Fangqing as a youth was sharp and well read.

s0114.literal: When grown, he had capacity and strategy.
s0114.idiomatic: As an adult he showed ability and foresight.

s0115.literal: In the Tiankang era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru county.
s0115.idiomatic: During Tiankang he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linru.

s0116.literal: Soon he was made Supervising Censor, Tutor to the Crown Prince, acting concurrently as Director of the Imperial Clan, and assigned to the Direct Palace Office.
s0116.idiomatic: He was soon made supervising censor and tutor to the crown prince, acting director of the imperial clan, and posted to the Direct Palace Office.

s0117.literal: In the ninth year of Taijian he went out as General of the Light Chariot, acting bearer of the staff, Area Commander over Military Affairs in Dingzhou, and Inspector of Dingzhou.
s0117.idiomatic: In Taijian year nine he was sent out as general of the light chariot, acting bearer of the staff, commander of armies in Dingzhou, and inspector of the province.

s0118.literal: When his term ended, he again became Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan.
s0118.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned as regular attendant of the Secretariat and again directed the imperial clan.

s0119.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was advanced in title to General of Intelligent Martial Might and Inspector of Wuzhou.
s0119.idiomatic: In Zhide year two he was promoted to general of intelligent martial might and inspector of Wuzhou.

s0120.literal: Earlier, Ma Jing, Inspector of Guangzhou, had long dwelt south of the ranges, won great favor among the people, and had strong troops and horses; the court was suspicious of him.
s0120.idiomatic: Ma Jing had long governed Guangzhou in the far south, won the people's loyalty, and commanded a strong force; the court grew wary of him.

s0121.literal: Thereupon Fangqing was made General of Benevolent Might and Inspector of Guangzhou and sent with troops to attack Jing.
s0121.idiomatic: Fangqing was then made general of benevolent might and inspector of Guangzhou and sent to attack Ma Jing with an army.

s0122.literal: When Jing was executed, Fangqing was advanced in title to General Who Proclaims Resolution.
s0122.idiomatic: After Jing was killed, Fangqing was promoted to general who proclaims resolution.

s0123.literal: Fangqing's nature was pure and careful, and he won great harmony among the people.
s0123.idiomatic: Fangqing was upright and cautious and governed with popular support.

s0124.literal: In year four he was advanced in title to General of the Cloud Banner.
s0124.idiomatic: In year four he was promoted to general of the cloud banner.

s0125.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, Sui forces crossed the Yangzi; [Eastern] Hengzhou Inspector Wang Yong sent Dai Zhilie, Inspector of Gaozhou, with five hundred cavalry to welcome Fangqing, [8] intending to have him take emergency command as overall commander of the armies for suppression and attack.
s0125.idiomatic: In Zhenming year three, as Sui crossed the Yangzi, [Eastern] Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong sent Gaozhou inspector Dai Zhilie with five hundred horsemen to fetch Fangqing, [8] planning to put him at the head of all southern armies.

s0126.literal: At that time Sui's campaign commander Wei Guang led troops across the ranges and proclaimed an edict of Emperor Wen of Sui, saying: "If Lingnan is pacified, Yong and Zheng Wanqing, Inspector of Fengzhou, are to remain in their former posts.
s0126.idiomatic: Sui commander Wei Guang then crossed the mountains with an edict from Emperor Wen of Sui: if Lingnan were pacified, Yong and Fengzhou inspector Zheng Wanqing would keep their posts.

s0127.literal: " When Fangqing heard this, he feared Yong would sell him out; he would not obey and led troops to resist Zhilie.
s0127.idiomatic: Fangqing feared Yong meant to betray him, refused, and marched against Zhilie.

s0128.literal: Zhilie fought him, defeated him, beheaded Fangqing at Guangzhou, and captured his wife and children.
s0128.idiomatic: Zhilie defeated him, killed Fangqing at Guangzhou, and took his family prisoner.

s0129.literal: Wang Yong, in the Taijian era was Administrator of Jinling and had a reputation for ability in office.
s0129.idiomatic: Wang Yong had served as Jinling administrator in the Taijian era and was known as an able official.

s0130.literal: When Fangqing attacked Ma Jing, the court made Yong Super Martial General, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, and concurrent Interior Magistrate of Shixing, to lend weight to Fangqing's campaign.
s0130.idiomatic: When Fangqing moved against Ma Jing, the court made Yong super martial general, inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, and interior magistrate of Shixing to strengthen Fangqing's position.

s0131.literal: When Jing was executed, Yong was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longyang county for merit.
s0131.idiomatic: After Jing's death Yong was enfeoffed as viscount of Longyang for his service.

s0132.literal: When Sui armies reached the Yangzi, an edict appointed Yong Bearer of the Staff, Guang Victorious General, overall commander of military affairs in the twenty-four provinces of Heng, Guang, Jiao, Gui, Wu, and others, and General Who Pacifies the Yue, and he was to enter as reinforcement.
s0132.idiomatic: As Sui reached the river, Yong was made bearer of the staff, guang victorious general, commander of twenty-four southern provinces including Heng and Guang, and general who pacifies the Yue, and ordered north to reinforce the capital.

s0133.literal: When the capital fell, Yong thereupon issued proclamations within his jurisdiction, gathered troops to hold the land, and sent his uterine younger brother Deng Hao to lead five thousand men and encamp on the ridge.
s0133.idiomatic: When the capital fell Yong issued calls to arms, mustered troops to hold Lingnan, and sent his younger brother Deng Hao with five thousand men to camp on the pass.

s0134.literal: He also sent envoys to welcome Fangqing, wishing to borrow his name while himself holding the military keys.
s0134.idiomatic: He also sent for Fangqing, hoping to use his royal name while keeping command himself.

s0135.literal: When Fangqing was defeated, Yong captured his wife and children, seized his property, and divided it among his commanders.
s0135.idiomatic: After Fangqing's defeat Yong seized his family and goods and shared the loot among his generals.

s0136.literal: He also ordered his generals Wang Zhongxuan and Zeng Xiaowu to welcome Prince Boxin of Hengyang, Inspector of Western Hengzhou; Boxin was afraid and fled to Qingyuan commandery, and Xiaowu pursued and killed him.
s0136.idiomatic: He sent Wang Zhongxuan and Zeng Xiaowu to fetch Prince Boxin of Hengyang, inspector of Western Hengzhou; the prince fled to Qingyuan and Xiaowu ran him down and killed him.

s0137.literal: At that time Wei Guang's troops had already crossed the ridge; Zheng Wanqing, Inspector of Fengzhou, held the province and did not answer Yong's summons, while the Gaoliang woman
s0137.idiomatic: Wei Guang had already crossed the mountains; Fengzhou inspector Zheng Wanqing held his province and ignored Yong's call, while the Gaoliang woman

s0139.literal: [Xi] clan raised troops to respond to the Sui army, [9] attacked and captured neighboring commanderies; Yong had no plan left and thereupon surrendered with his host.
s0139.idiomatic: [Xi] raised troops for Sui, [9] overran neighboring districts; with no options left Yong surrendered with his army.

s0140.literal: En route at Jingzhou he fell ill on the road and died; Sui posthumously made him Grand General, Inspector of Songzhou, and Duke of Guiren county.
s0140.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road at Jingzhou and died; Sui posthumously made him grand general, Songzhou inspector, and duke of Guiren.

s0141.literal: Zheng Wanqing was a man of Xingyang, a clansman of Zheng Shaoshu, Inspector of Sizhou in Liang.
s0141.idiomatic: Zheng Wanqing of Xingyang was a kinsman of Liang's Sizhou inspector Zheng Shaoshu.

s0142.literal: His father Min entered Wei at the end of Liang.
s0142.idiomatic: His father Min went over to Northern Wei at the end of Liang.

s0143.literal: Wanqing was penetrating and capable; under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Metropolitan Construction Officer and went out as Inspector of Wenzhou.
s0143.idiomatic: Wanqing was talented and capable; under Zhou Emperor Wu he was metropolitan construction officer and later inspector of Wenzhou.

s0144.literal: In the Zhide era he came to Chen together with Sima Xiaonan.
s0144.idiomatic: In the Zhide era he defected to Chen with Sima Xiaonan.

s0145.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, General Who Manifests Martiality, and Inspector of Fengzhou.
s0145.idiomatic: He was soon made regular attendant, general who manifests martiality, and inspector of Fengzhou.

s0146.literal: In the province he had very benevolent government; officials and people memorialized requesting a stele, and an edict approved it.
s0146.idiomatic: He governed Fengzhou with real kindness; the people petitioned for a commemorative stele and the court agreed.

s0147.literal: Earlier, when Wanqing was in Zhou, he was deeply favored by Emperor Wen of Sui; when Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he often thought of returning north.
s0147.idiomatic: In Zhou he had been close to the future Sui founder; once Sui was founded he often wished to return north.

s0148.literal: When Yong killed Fangqing, Wanqing thereupon led the provincial troops to resist Yong and sent envoys by a secret route to surrender to the Sui army.
s0148.idiomatic: After Yong killed Fangqing, Wanqing marched against him and sent envoys by a hidden route to surrender to Sui.

s0149.literal: He was appointed Senior Dignitary of the First Rank; soon he died.
s0149.idiomatic: Sui made him a senior dignitary of the first rank; he died soon after.

s0150.literal: The historian says: The two princes Xian and Min, linked in splendor in the heavens—one intimate as an earth-son, one favored as like a son—yet the narrow bridge blocked them and the paired carriage team had no way; separated in a good age, they ended in early death.
s0150.idiomatic: The historian writes: Princes Xian and Min shone like stars in the sky—one a true brother's son, one cherished like a son—yet barriers kept them apart and they never came home; cut off in a fortunate age, both died young.

s0153.literal: truly relied on Xing and Wei—on "shi": the Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions read "shi" style/ceremony.
s0153.idiomatic: On "truly relied on Xing and Wei": the character shi—Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions read shi as ceremonial.

s0154.literal: Tiger guards with a hundred halberd-bearers—"Tiger guard" is "Tiger Brave," changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0154.idiomatic: On "tiger guards, a hundred halberd-bearers": tiger guard renders huben, taboo-avoiding for Tang.

s0155.literal: The Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions have all already been changed to "Tiger Brave."
s0155.idiomatic: Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions already read tiger brave.

s0156.literal: at the time [aged] twenty-eight—supplied according to the Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.
s0156.idiomatic: On "at the time [aged] twenty-eight": supplied from Northern Supervisor, Ji, and Palace editions.

s0157.literal: Area Commander over Military Affairs in the nineteen provinces of Guang, Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Ming, Xin, He, Luo, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Jian, Shiya, and others—counting them there are only eighteen provinces; it is suspected one province is missing, or "nine" should read "eight."
s0157.idiomatic: On the nineteen-province command: the list counts only eighteen; one province may be missing, or nine may be an error for eight.

s0158.literal: Emperor Xuan ascended the Xuanwu Gate tower—"tower" in the Ji and Palace editions reads "in person," belonging to the following clause.
s0158.idiomatic: On "Emperor Xuan ascended the Xuanwu Gate tower": Ji and Palace read in person, attaching it to the next phrase.

s0162.literal: The tower is the tower on the Xuanwu Gate."
s0162.idiomatic: It means the viewing tower on Xuanwu Gate."

s0163.literal: According to the Northern Supervisor edition it reads "tower"; the Baibaina edition of the History of the Southern Dynasties also reads "tower."
s0163.idiomatic: The Northern Supervisor text reads tower; the Baibaina Southern Dynasties history agrees.

s0164.literal: Thereupon the acting censor-in-chief Xu Junfu memorialized—"Xu Junfu" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xu Junzheng."
s0164.idiomatic: On "acting censor-in-chief Xu Junfu memorialized": the Southern Dynasties history reads Xu Junzheng.

s0167.literal: [autumn] office—changed according to the Imperial Mirror 519.
s0167.idiomatic: On "[autumn] office": emended per the Imperial Mirror 519.

s0168.literal: [Eastern] Hengzhou Inspector Wang Yong sent Dai Zhilie, Inspector of Gaozhou, with five hundred cavalry to welcome Fangqing—supplied according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0168.idiomatic: On "[Eastern] Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong sent Gaozhou inspector Dai Zhilie with five hundred cavalry to welcome Fangqing": supplied from the Southern Dynasties history.

s0169.literal: Comment: below it says "the court made Yong Super Martial General, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou"—clearly one character "Eastern" is missing here.
s0169.idiomatic: Below the text calls Yong inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, so dong (eastern) is missing here.

s0172.literal: [Xi] clan raised troops to respond to the Sui army—the Biography of Wei Guang in the Book of Sui reads "the Gaoliang woman Xi clan"; the Comprehensive Mirror, Kaihuang year nine of Emperor Wen of Sui, reads "the Grand Mistress Xi of Gaoliang commandery"; "Hao" and "Xi" are alike in form and corrupt—now changed accordingly.
s0172.idiomatic: On "[Xi] clan raised troops for Sui": the Book of Sui biography of Wei Guang has Lady Xi of Gaoliang; the Comprehensive Mirror (Kaihuang 9) has Grand Mistress Xi of Gaoliang; hao and xi are graphically similar—emended accordingly.
